requirements.note: History shows the newest workout first, in inset-grouped sections by month. Each row has the name, date, exercise count and volume (e.g. Legs, Sun Oct 25, 4 exercises · 6,767.5 lb). A + in the nav bar also starts a workout.
Detail has a large title, a summary card (exercises, sets, volume) and one section per exercise listing its sets with a per-exercise volume footer. Each exercise header links to its exercise screen.

Name the workout, then pick exercises in a multi-select sheet with a native search field and muscle filter chips ('Add (2)'). Sets open in a sheet with reps/weight fields and steppers, pre-filled from last time, with inline validation (Save disabled, red message). Tap a set to edit it, swipe to delete. Finish asks for confirmation, warns that exercises with no sets will be left out, saves to History and switches to it. Shows a timer and 'Last time' hints.
Library tab is grouped by muscle with section headers, and pulling down reveals a search field.
Shows muscle and equipment, the best set (heaviest weight, with workout and date), and the workouts it appears in with their sets. It updated after finishing a new workout (102.5 lb × 10).
The in-progress workout (name, exercises, edited and deleted sets, timer) survived a relaunch, and so did the finished workout in History.

bugs: On an exercise's screen opened from a workout, the first row under Workouts stays highlighted grey (shown as selected) after the push and never clears.
tells: The Finish/Discard confirmation is a popover whose arrow points at the summary text rather than at the Finish button.
The reps field (on a number pad) accepts non-numeric characters typed from a hardware keyboard; validation catches it, though.
A.scroll: History (61 rows) and Library (120 rows) scroll like native lists: smooth drags and flings, sticky month and muscle headers, no blank or popping rows. Tapping the tab returns to the top, and scroll position is kept after pushing to a detail and back.

requirements.note: History lists workouts newest first in one inset-grouped section, with name, date, exercise count and volume (no month grouping).
Detail has a Date/Exercises/Sets/Volume summary and one section per exercise listing 'Set n  reps × weight'. Exercises do not link to their exercise screen.

Start Workout shows an alert to enter the name. Add Exercise opens a single-select sheet with a bottom search bar and a Muscle menu picker. Add Set opens a sheet with Reps/Weight fields, pre-filled from the previous set. Tap a set to edit it, swipe to delete it (and swipe an exercise to remove it). Finish saves to History with no confirmation. There are no bounds on input: it accepted 585 reps × 707,060 lb.
Library tab is grouped by muscle, with a search field revealed on pull-down.
Shows the best set (heaviest weight, with reps, workout and date), muscle and equipment, and 'Workouts · N' with the best set in each. The new workout appeared there.
The in-progress workout and the finished workout both survived a relaunch.

bugs: At the largest text size, the New Set/Edit Set sheet header breaks: the title wraps onto two lines and overlaps the exercise name below it, and the Add/Save button is pushed off the right edge of the screen.
No limits on set values: absurd reps and weights (585 × 707,060 lb) are accepted and pollute volume totals.
tells: The Set sheet's header is hand-drawn and differs from every other sheet: plain blue 'Cancel' text instead of a glass button, a large regular-weight title that is not centred, a grey capsule for Add/Save, and no grabber.
The search field in the exercise picker (a bottom search bar) does not show up in the accessibility tree.
The active workout repeats its large-title name in a 'Name' row directly below the title.
The empty Workout tab places the Start Workout button at the very bottom, far from the empty-state message.
Generic tab icons (calendar, ECG waveform, book) for History, Workout and Library.
The exercise picker adds one exercise per opening, so adding several means reopening the sheet each time.
B.scroll: History and Library scroll smoothly with native deceleration and no blank or popping rows. Tapping the tab returns to the top, and scroll position is kept after pushing to a detail and back.

why: Both apps meet every requirement and scroll natively. A's workout flow is richer and more careful: multi-select picker with filter chips, steppers, validated input, a finish confirmation, and links from a workout to each exercise. B's set sheet has a hand-built header that looks off-platform and breaks at the largest text size, and B accepts nonsense set values.
